title: Chess AI & Multiplayer
description: Implement minimax with alpha-beta pruning, design evaluation functions, build WebSocket-based real-time play, and implement the Elo rating system.

segments.text: Minimax is the foundation of chess AI. Build a game tree: your turn maximizes the score, opponent's turn minimizes it. Search to a fixed depth — say six plies. At leaf nodes, evaluate the position. Propagate scores up: max at your nodes, min at opponent's nodes. The root's best child is the move to play. Deep Blue searched twelve plies or more.

Alpha-beta pruning cuts the game tree dramatically. Alpha is the minimum score you're guaranteed. Beta is the maximum score the opponent allows. If a branch can't improve alpha or worsen beta, prune it. With perfect move ordering, alpha-beta reduces the effective branching factor from thirty-five to about six — searching twice as deep in the same time.

The evaluation function scores a position without searching further. Material count: pawn equals one, knight and bishop equal three, rook equals five, queen equals nine. But position matters: a knight in the center controls eight squares, on the edge only four. Piece-square tables give bonuses based on position. Add king safety, pawn structure, and mobility for a strong evaluator.

Alpha-beta's efficiency depends on checking the best moves first. Use iterative deepening: search depth one, then two, then three. Use the previous depth's best move as the first move at the next depth. Also try captures before quiet moves, and killer moves — moves that caused cutoffs in sibling nodes. Good ordering prunes ninety percent of the tree.
Your chess engine searches six plies deep in two seconds. The opponent has three minutes per move. How would you use the remaining two minutes and fifty-eight seconds to improve the move quality?
segments.thought_prompt: How would you use iterative deepening to maximize search depth within a time limit?

segments.text: Real-time multiplayer uses WebSocket for bidirectional communication. Each game has a room. When player A makes a move, the server validates it, updates game state, and pushes the move to player B's WebSocket. Server-side validation is non-negotiable — never trust the client for move legality. Cheating detection compares client moves against server-validated legal moves.

Chess clocks are server-authoritative. Track each player's remaining time on the server. When a player moves, stop their clock and start the opponent's. Increment systems add seconds per move. If a player's time reaches zero, they lose. Never rely on client-reported time — latency compensation is needed. Subtract average round-trip time from the player's used time.

The Elo rating system quantifies player strength. Expected score: one divided by one plus ten to the power of rating-difference divided by four hundred. After a game, adjust ratings: new equals old plus K times actual minus expected. K factor is thirty-two for new players, sixteen for established ones. A two hundred point difference means the higher-rated player wins seventy-five percent of the time.

Matchmaking pairs players with similar Elo ratings. Start with a narrow range — plus or minus fifty points. If no match in thirty seconds, widen to one hundred. Continue widening up to three hundred. Track queue wait times and adjust dynamically. Chess.com processes over ten million games per day using this adaptive matchmaking.

Design the multiplayer architecture for an online chess platform supporting one hundred thousand concurrent games with move latency under two hundred milliseconds. What's your WebSocket server architecture?
segments.thought_prompt: Design multiplayer chess for 100K concurrent games with sub-200ms move latency.

segments.text: Chess AI uses minimax with alpha-beta pruning and carefully tuned evaluation functions. Multiplayer requires WebSocket-based real-time communication with server-authoritative validation and time control. Elo ratings provide fair matchmaking. The design challenge is combining the AI engine, multiplayer infrastructure, and rating system into a cohesive platform.
